description:
MAINTAINER POINT, recorded 2026-08-11: porting the DWSIM dynamics gets a TRANSIENT simulator, not a REAL-TIME one. These are different problems and the port does not solve the second.

WHY: DWSIM Integrator.vb advances simulated time as fast or as slow as the solve happens to take. Each step calls flash and property evaluations of unbounded cost, and a stiff or poorly converging step can take arbitrarily long. Real-time requires bounded worst-case wall-clock per step, which nothing in the upstream provides.

WHAT MUST BE SETTLED:
1. Define the target. Soft real-time for an interactive twin (drop or interpolate on overrun) or hard bounded step. These have very different costs.
2. Measure first. Instrument the ported transient loop for per-step wall-clock, worst case not mean, before designing anything. op-fm5 is the precedent: a 28 us/step plateau was MEASURED in TUAS and drove a rewrite to O(1) recurrences.
3. The likely cost centres are flash calls in the inner loop and the recycle/pressure-flow convergence iteration count, both of which are unbounded by construction.
4. Candidate strategies, to be chosen on evidence not assumption: cache or tabulate property evaluations, fix the iteration budget and carry the residual forward, precompute reduced-order surrogates for slow blocks, or run the rigorous model off the real-time thread and pace a reduced model against it.
5. See docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md, which already frames the multi-fidelity approach for this workspace.

ACCEPTANCE: a measured per-step cost distribution from the actual ported loop, a stated real-time target, and one recorded decision on strategy. Do not claim real-time capability without a measured worst-case number.
title: refinery: DECISION — real-time execution, which DWSIM dynamics does NOT give you

description: Blender's Spin. Sweep a profile polyline around an arbitrary axis (point + direction) by an angle in N segments (Rodrigues rotation), connecting consecutive rings with quads. Full 360deg closes the seam (wrap), a partial angle leaves it open. Off-axis profile points only in v1 (on-axis pole points documented as needing a subsequent weld). Generates pipes/tubes/vessels/cones -- surfaces of revolution, on-theme for reactor geometry. Free generator fn (like primitives), not a MeshOp. V&V: a 2-point off-axis segment revolved 360deg/16 -> open 16-gon tube V32 F16 chi0; fill_holes(that) -> closed prism chi2 with positive volume ~ 16-gon*height; a partial 180deg sweep leaves an open strip.
title: outram-blender: revolve / spin (surface of revolution)
